intended_object: The map pr₀* : ∏_{f:V→U in R} P(V) → ∏_{(f,g)} P(V ×_U W) from the equalizer diagram of the sheaf condition (Stacks 00VM). On the (f,g) factor it is the projection to P(V) followed by restriction along the first pullback projection V ×_U W → V. Inferred from the docstring and the Stacks tag.
explanation:
The definition uses `Pi.lift`. For each index (f, g) it takes the projection `Pi.π` onto the factor P(V) of `firstObj`, then composes with `P.map (pullback.fst f g).op`. This is exactly Stacks' pr₀* for a presheaf with values in a category A that has products.

It is stated in natural generality:
- A is an arbitrary category with products of the needed size.
- C is any category with pullbacks.
- R is any presieve.

The Type-valued version in Mathlib, `Equalizer.Presieve.firstMap`, is a special case of this one, not a broader form of it. So the definition is faithful.
